files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.ControlReferenceImage

The image of the control reference image is either a control image provided by the user, or a regular image which the backend will use to generate a control image of. In the case of the latter, the enable_control_image_computation field in the config should be set to True. A control image is an image that represents a sketch image of areas for the model to fill in based on the prompt.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.FunctionDeclaration
files.Summary: Structured representation of a function declaration as defined by the OpenAPI 3.0 specification (https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.0.3). Included in this declaration are the function name, description, parameters and response type. This FunctionDeclaration is a representation of a block of code that can be used as a Tool by the model and executed by the client.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.FunctionResponse
files.Summary: The result output from a FunctionCall that contains a string representing the FunctionDeclaration.name and a structured JSON object containing any output from the function is used as context to the model. This should contain the result of a FunctionCall made based on model prediction.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.FunctionResponseBlob
files.Summary: Raw media bytes for function response. Text should not be sent as raw bytes, use the 'text' field.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.FunctionResponseFileData
files.Summary: URI based data for function response. This data type is not supported in Gemini API.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.FunctionResponsePart
files.Summary: A datatype containing media that is part of a FunctionResponse message. A FunctionResponsePart consists of data which has an associated datatype. A FunctionResponsePart can only contain one of the accepted types in FunctionResponsePart.data. A FunctionResponsePart must have a fixed IANA MIME type identifying the type and subtype of the media if the inline_data field is filled with raw bytes.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.FunctionResponseScheduling
files.Summary: Specifies how the response should be scheduled in the conversation. Only applicable to NON_BLOCKING function calls, is ignored otherwise. Defaults to WHEN_IDLE.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GcsSource

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GenerateContentResponsePromptFeedback
files.Summary: Content filter results for a prompt sent in the request. Note: This is sent only in the first stream chunk and only if no candidates were generated due to content violations.

files.Summary: The configuration for automated routing. When automated routing is specified, the routing will be determined by the pretrained routing model and customer provided model routing preference. This data type is not supported in Gemini API.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GoogleRpcStatus
files.Summary: The Status type defines a logical error model that is suitable for different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is used by gRPC (https://github.com/grpc). Each Status message contains three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details. You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the API Design Guide (https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors). This data type is not supported in Gemini API.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GoogleSearch
files.Summary: GoogleSearch tool type. Tool to support Google Search in Model. Powered by Google.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GoogleSearchRetrieval
files.Summary: Tool to retrieve public web data for grounding, powered by Google.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GoogleTypeDate
files.Summary: Represents a whole or partial calendar date, such as a birthday. The time of day and time zone are either specified elsewhere or are insignificant. The date is relative to the Gregorian Calendar. This can represent one of the following: * A full date, with non-zero year, month, and day values. * A month and day, with a zero year (for example, an anniversary). * A year on its own, with a zero month and a zero day. * A year and month, with a zero day (for example, a credit card expiration date). Related types: * google.type.TimeOfDay * google.type.DateTime * google.protobuf.Timestamp. This data type is not supported in Gemini API.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunk
files.Summary: A piece of evidence that supports a claim made by the model. This is used to show a citation for a claim made by the model. When grounding is enabled, the model returns a GroundingChunk that contains a reference to the source of the information.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkCustomMetadata
files.Summary: User provided metadata about the GroundingFact. This data type is not supported in Vertex AI.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkImage
files.Summary: An Image chunk is a piece of evidence that comes from an image search result. It contains the URI of the image search result and the URI of the image. This is used to provide the user with a link to the source of the information.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkMaps
files.Summary: A Maps chunk is a piece of evidence that comes from Google Maps. It contains information about a place, such as its name, address, and reviews. This is used to provide the user with rich, location-based information.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkMapsPlaceAnswerSources
files.Summary: The sources that were used to generate the place answer. This includes review snippets and photos that were used to generate the answer, as well as URIs to flag content.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkMapsPlaceAnswerSourcesAuthorAttribution

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkMapsPlaceAnswerSourcesReviewSnippet

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkMapsRoute
files.Summary: Route information from Google Maps. This data type is not supported in Gemini API.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkRetrievedContext
files.Summary: Context retrieved from a data source to ground the model's response. This is used when a retrieval tool fetches information from a user-provided corpus or a public dataset.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkStringList
files.Summary: A list of string values. This data type is not supported in Vertex AI.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingChunkWeb
files.Summary: A Web chunk is a piece of evidence that comes from a web page. It contains the URI of the web page, the title of the page, and the domain of the page. This is used to provide the user with a link to the source of the information.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.GroundingMetadata

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.LiveClientContent
files.Summary: Incremental update of the current conversation delivered from the client. All the content here will unconditionally be appended to the conversation history and used as part of the prompt to the model to generate content. A message here will interrupt any current model generation.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.LiveClientRealtimeInput
files.Summary: User input that is sent in real time. This is different from LiveClientContent in a few ways: - Can be sent continuously without interruption to model generation. - If there is a need to mix data interleaved across the LiveClientContent and the LiveClientRealtimeInput, server attempts to optimize for best response, but there are no guarantees. - End of turn is not explicitly specified, but is rather derived from user activity (for example, end of speech). - Even before the end of turn, the data is processed incrementally to optimize for a fast start of the response from the model. - Is always assumed to be the user's input (cannot be used to populate conversation history).

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.LiveClientToolResponse

Note that in the unary and server-streaming GenerateContent APIs function calling happens by exchanging the Content parts, while in the bidi GenerateContent APIs function calling happens over this dedicated set of messages.

files.Title: Google.GenAI.Types.LogprobsResult
files.Summary: The log probabilities of the tokens generated by the model. This is useful for understanding the model's confidence in its predictions and for debugging. For example, you can use log probabilities to identify when the model is making a less confident prediction or to explore alternative responses that the model considered. A low log probability can also indicate that the model is "hallucinating" or generating factually incorrect information.
